size.note: Newman's Birds gives 20 cm. Wikipedia gives an average of 21 cm.

habitat: Almost any well-developed woodland, including Acacia and Mopane, and mixed bushveld. It prefers relatively mesic woodland for breeding, often riverine, nesting in a tunnel in a sand or clay bank. Non-breeding migrants also use degraded bushveld and even sewage works.
summary: A summer visitor to woodland, with a grey head and breast, a chestnut belly, deep blue wings and tail, black on the upper back and shoulders, and a red bill. It is not very vocal. Newman's calls the mantle grey and the back royal blue; Wikipedia says the mantle and back are black with a bright blue rump. Photographs checked for this page show a black upper back and a blue rump, and the marks follow that. The front photograph and both recordings are from Kenya (nominate race), not the southern race. The juvenile photograph is from Benin.

similar.note: Brown-hooded is larger and has a streaked brown head and streaked buffy breast and flanks with no chestnut belly. In flight its underwings are all cinnamon; Grey-headed's are white and rufous (Newman's; eBird).

viewNotes.note: Front-on, the grey head and breast sit above a chestnut belly, with a red bill (Newman's; eBird).

From behind, the upper back and shoulders are black and the rump, wings and tail are blue. Newman's calls the mantle grey and the back royal blue; Wikipedia says the mantle and back are black with a bright blue rump.
Side-on, the black wing-coverts show against the blue flight feathers (Newman's).

calls.description: Not very vocal: a weak, descending 'chi-chi-chi-chi' (Newman's); a strident trilling 't-t-t-t-t-t-t' and a repeated, squeaky 'tsury, tsury' (eBird); a warning call, a series of sharp 'tchk' notes (Wikipedia). SABAP1 notes that non-breeding migrants can be silent and easily overlooked. Both recordings are from Kenya (nominate race), not southern Africa.
